headline: edio fixes AI coding agent Git issues in under 5 milliseconds
summary: New tool edio creates an isolated Shadow Commit DAG to prevent AI agents from breaking your codebase, offering micro-versioning safety without disrupting your workflow.
details: AI coding agents can be a double-edged sword. While they assist in writing code, they can also introduce regressions and break imports, especially after multiple iterations. This is a common frustration for developers using tools like Claude Code or Cursor.

edio is a new tool designed to tackle this problem. It operates as a single Go binary that integrates directly into your existing .git folder, creating an isolated 'Shadow Commit DAG' visible only to edio. This allows it to take invisible snapshots of your code after each agent edit.

The tool bypasses standard Git commands like 'git add' and 'git commit' by working directly with low-level Git primitives. This isolation prevents agent snapshots from overwriting your staging index or moving your HEAD, preserving your current work.

edio uses 'git commit-tree' to link agent turns together without creating temporary branches or moving HEAD. The shadow DAG is kept invisible to standard Git commands like 'git log' and 'git branch', ensuring your main commit history remains clean.

This approach provides the safety of micro-versioning, allowing developers to easily revert agent-induced changes, while maintaining the cleanliness of a single, linear commit history. It also offers built-in support for AI coding assistants and templates for quick answers or snippets.

headline_marked: LG [[denies continuous TV audio recording]] amid privacy concerns
headline: LG denies continuous TV audio recording amid privacy concerns
summary: LG claims its smart TVs do not continuously record or transmit user conversations, stating wake-word detection is processed locally. However, researchers found extensive logs of ambient conversations.
details: LG is responding to allegations that its smart TVs are capturing and uploading user audio data. The company asserts that reports of continuous recording are misleading.

LG states that its TVs do not "continuously record or transmit users’ conversations," and that wake-word detection is processed locally on the device. This comes after researchers detailed findings of extensive logging of ambient conversations.

The company also clarified that features like Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) and voice recognition are optional and not enabled by default. ACR uses audio fingerprinting to identify content and does not collect screenshots, screen recordings, or voice recordings.

However, LG did not address broader concerns regarding the extent of data collection, data sharing practices, potential vulnerabilities for exploitation by bad actors, or the clarity of its privacy option presentation.
